blocks.text: Shape before magnitude
What the field looks like before anyone agrees on severity
The market publishes hazard scores and line-cards. Nobody publishes this plane. The scatter is what you get when you stop ranking breakage and start reading posture.

This slice scores {{fact:total}} entities across {{fact:n_layers}} layers — {{fact:l1}} carriers, {{fact:l2}} MGAs and brokers, {{fact:l3}} assets, {{fact:l4}} in the tail — while live registers still load. Only {{fact:measured_pct}} of the weight rests on measured evidence, so what follows is a provisional read of structure, not a published league table. The question is not yet who wins. It is whether exposure and preparedness actually separate once you plot them on the same axes.

Read the stat row the way an investor reads a services map: where is the mass, where is the minority that matters, how wide is the spread. {{fact:earning_count}} entities ({{fact:earning_pct}}) sit in Earning it — exposed and prepared enough to carry the bet. {{fact:sidelined_count}} ({{fact:sidelined_pct}}) sit in Sidelined, watching from the bench. The minority that should concentrate attention is Exposed: {{fact:exposed_count}} names ({{fact:exposed_pct}}) where non-firm load has outrun product fit, register literacy or capital depth. That is where connection agreements and BI wordings diverge in the data, not where headline premium concentrates.

A damage-first read would mostly approve this field. Earning it plus Sidelined account for most of the universe because physical-damage capacity and rating-agency capital look fine on paper. The construct is built to find the names that look fine on damage and are not fine on availability — the same blind spot a hazard score hides when it collapses two axes into one rank.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI}}

blocks.caption: Distribution of the current universe across the four quadrants, on median cut-lines (exposure ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, preparedness ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}).

blocks.text: The margin spread is {{fact:mos_spread}} points against a median of {{fact:median_mos}}. Posture, not pedigree, separates the tails. At one end, {{fact:top_mos_name}} shows preparedness — capital, specialist product, data — currently outrunning non-firm exposure on the book. At the other, {{fact:low_mos_name}} at {{fact:low_mos_val}} shows exposure that has outrun the means to carry it. Neither tail is a moral verdict on the firm. Both are a mismatch question: does the bet still match the balance sheet and the wording on file.

Whitespace is the commercial hinge in the data: {{fact:whitespace_count}} entities ({{fact:whitespace_pct}}) high on preparedness, low on exposure. That is judgement surplus in a market still running intelligence-heavy placement on damage forms — rated capital, broker infrastructure and specialist product not yet routed onto availability risk. {{fact:top_whitespace_name}} is representative: preparation on the balance sheet, negligible availability premium in the disclosed book. The deployment question is autopilot timing: who moves first from could write register-native cover to is writing it before queue repricing closes the window.{{cite:ACAD-CLARKE-INDEX-DEMAND,SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL,INSTECH-NDBI-PARAMETRIC}}
Two surfaces in the data
Placement posture above, register facts below

The same policy failure shows up differently depending on where you sit in the chain. Exposed concentrates in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}} — structurally right, because non-firm intensity is a register fact at Layer 3 before it propagates to carriers and reinsurers. Layer 1 contributes {{fact:exposed_l1}} Exposed names and Layer 2 contributes {{fact:exposed_l2}} where concentration outruns trigger fit on the facilities they bind. Layer 4 shows {{fact:exposed_l4}} Exposed so far: tail capacity that may not yet see grid correlation the primary market misses.{{cite:NESO-TEC,ACT-HHI-EIOPA}}

Carriers and intermediaries cluster in Whitespace ({{fact:whitespace_l1}} at Layer 1, {{fact:whitespace_l2}} at Layer 2) more than in Exposed because balance-sheet preparedness is easier to evidence from filings than curtailment exposure is to see from the outside. That asymmetry is the whole intelligence-versus-judgement split in one chart: registers and schedules are intelligence work the market outsources poorly; carrying correlated availability tail is judgement work it has not priced yet.

With only {{fact:measured_pct}} measured share, treat rank order inside a quadrant as soft and layer skew as harder signal. Magnitudes at the asset layer will move as Gate 2 records land; the finding that L3 leads Exposed should survive register refresh because firmness lives in the connection offer first.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}
Running hot on exposure
Where the bet outruns the tower

Within Exposed, the deepest negative gap belongs to {{fact:worst_exposed_name}} — flexible-connection or concentrated energy exposure without a matching availability line on the file. {{fact:exposed_l3}} of {{fact:exposed_count}} Exposed names are assets: curtailment rights in the connection agreement precede mitigation evidence in the tower. Of {{fact:l3_total}} scored campuses, {{fact:gate_firm_count}} carry firm Gate status in the register and {{fact:gate_unknown_count}} remain unknown. The index reports both and infers neither — unknown is provisional honesty, not a hidden imputation.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-TEC}}

Picture the claims surface this scatter anticipates. A curtailment becomes a BI notification. Adjusters cross-reference schedules box by box while the operator log shows lawful switch-off with no damage event. The data here is the placement-side mirror: names already in Exposed before that workflow runs, because exposure was visible in registers the premium function never read. One industry, two bottlenecks, the same missing trigger visible from opposite ends of the chain.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,INSTECH-NDBI-PARAMETRIC}}

The headline is not who ranks first. It is that exposure and preparedness come apart across {{fact:total}} entities and {{fact:mos_spread}} points of margin spread — which is why a one-axis hazard score misleads and a margin does not.
Honest about proof
What compounds when registers land

Only {{fact:measured_pct}} of the score rests on measured evidence today, so read magnitudes as direction. What moves as live data lands is ordering within quadrants: non-firm intensity from connection registers, capital from filings, trigger gaps from product schedules. Entities will shift across the median cut-lines (exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}) as those inputs firm up. What should not move is the construct — two axes, one margin, and the separation they reveal.

That compounding loop is the autopilot wedge in data form. Today's judgement calls on which names look mismatched become tomorrow's intelligence once register trails exist at scale — the same convergence Services describes for outsourced audit work. This section re-runs on every build against whatever the registers then say; the shape you see now is the argument the market has not yet published, not the final word on severity.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}}
